bull.b: Owned energized capacity and low blended electricity costs provide a durable operating foundation for Bitcoin mining, colocation, and future AI/HPC workloads. This infrastructure can support expansion while giving PowerCompute flexibility to monetize power through multiple compute businesses.

Securing 11 MW of contracted Columbus capacity through 2030 improves infrastructure visibility and supports sustained operating scale. Avoiding the stated TVA capacity levy and receiving a deposit refund should also preserve capital for site expansion without additional utility-funded capital contributions.

bull.t: Reduced Secured Debt and Collateral Burden
bull.b: Repaying the Bitcoin-backed facility materially reduces secured obligations and removes pledged-asset constraints. Eliminating associated interest and collar costs can improve financial flexibility, while retaining unpledged Bitcoin gives management more control over future capital deployment and operating investments.

bear.b: The recent income trajectory indicates that the business is not yet producing sustainable unit economics. Falling revenue combined with negative gross profit and exceptionally deep losses could limit reinvestment capacity, weaken resilience, and require a prolonged turnaround before earnings become dependable.

Substantial operating and free-cash-flow deficits show that current activities are not self-funding. Continued cash consumption can force reliance on asset sales, financing, or equity issuance, reducing strategic flexibility and making execution more difficult while the company builds newer compute businesses.

The AI/HPC strategy has not yet demonstrated material commercial traction, so its potential cannot currently offset weakness in the existing business. Scaling toward the illustrative revenue range depends on securing customers and capital, creating meaningful execution risk over the next several quarters.
